The methyl radical has a tetrahedral geometry, with the unpaired electron in the x-orbital. The x-orbital can be oriented in any direction in space, resulting in a total of 3 possible orientations (x, y, and z axes).

Since the lines in the EPR spectrum correspond to the different orientations of the unpaired electron, the number of lines is equal to the number of possible orientations. Therefore, the number of lines in the EPR spectrum of a solution of 13C-labelled methyl radical (13CH3•) is 3.
